headline: Show what everything is waiting on, and what will free it

V26-3552.title: Say what a story that hasn't started is waiting on

criteria.text: c1: A planned story whose after keys have not all landed says which story it waits on and where that story stands.
c2: A planned story whose files another lane holds says which lane and for which story.
c3: The lead can record why a story waits, and that reason is shown with the story.
c4: An idle lane whose next story is waiting is shown as waiting, with the same reason, not as stalled.
c5: When the wait ends, the reason goes away with no action from the lead.

V26-3426.title: Give a lane a "waiting on another story" state that the views show as progress, not as the operator's blocker

criteria.text: A lane waiting on another story's merge isn't in "Needs you" and doesn't hold the close, and the row clears when that story merges.
After lead-accept, the lane's row is no longer handed/blocked, waiting on the lead.

c3: Lane rows keep their order across writes: lead-assign replaces a lane's row in place rather than moving it to the end, so every view shows lanes in the record's declared order; and each lane's colour comes from its id, never its position, so lane 2 is always lane 2's colour.

V26-3555.title: Show a review round while it is running

criteria.text: c1: While a round runs, the story's review shows that round as under way, at the head being reviewed, with how long ago it started.
c2: The last finished round's outcome is shown with its candidate and how many commits the branch has moved since.
c3: Each lens of the running round shows as back, with its verdict, or still reading; a lens that returns updates in place with no reload.
c4: The lane's reason for the round is shown when it gave one, and nothing is shown when it did not.
c5: Earlier rounds' confirmed notes are folded while a round runs and open as they do today.
c6: When the round is reduced, the card settles to the finished round's card as it is today.
c7: A round restarted or abandoned does not leave a round shown as running.
c8: Nothing moves under reduced motion, and every looping motion keeps the page's shared tempo.

V26-3554.title: Show a wait on another delivery sharing the base, in both deliveries

criteria.text: c1: A story or lane that needs a shared file another delivery claims says which delivery holds it and for which story.
c2: A lead whose acceptance or push is held by another lead's check or tag on the shared base sees which delivery, what it is doing, and since when.
c3: The holding delivery shows which deliveries are waiting on its claim or check.
c4: Both sides read it from the same facts, in the shape the epic settles for "waits on".
c5: When the claim is released or the check ends, both sides clear with no action from either lead.

V26-3565.title: Catch a provenance listing change at hand-off, not in the merge queue
V26-3565.why: Restored: plan change c13 removed the whole story by mistake when the lead meant to remove only its criterion c3 (lead-plan change --kind removed ignores --criterion). The story stays in the delivery, decoupled from this repository at the operator's request

criteria.text: c1: A hand-off whose candidate adds or removes an output a regenerable listing names is refused when its lane doesn't own the listing file, naming the file, the outputs and the grant to ask for, and nothing is recorded.
c2: The same hand-off is accepted when the lane owns the listing file, and a hand-off that only refreshes digests is accepted for any lane.
c4: The lane brief names each regenerable listing the binding declares, and says that adding or removing an output it lists needs that file's owner; with no listings declared it says nothing.

V26-3566.title: Let lead-plan drop one criterion, and refuse a flag a change doesn't use
V26-3566.why: The operator asked to add it to this delivery: plan change c13 removed V26-3565 when the lead meant to drop one criterion, because lead-plan's removed kind ignores --criterion and no kind drops a single criterion

criteria.text: c1: A lead-plan change given a flag its kind doesn't use is refused, naming the flag, and nothing is written.
c2: --kind removed with --criterion drops only that criterion, records the change with its reason, and leaves the story and its other criteria in place.
c3: Dropping a criterion the story lacks, or its last one, is refused and nothing is written.
c4: The plan chapter shows the dropped criterion struck through, with its reason.

c5: The plan chapter states, in one sentence, the approved and current story counts and the stories and criteria added, removed and changed since approval, matching the recorded changes; with none, it says the scope is as approved.
c6: A finish line raised since approval shows that it was raised, from what to what, and when.
c7: A change added after approval is marked as not reviewed with the plan.

V26-3567.title: Show what needs someone as one list, in the lanes' own visual language
V26-3567.why: The operator approved a live mock of Needs you in the lanes' visual language, merged with Needs attention, and asked to add it to this delivery

criteria.text: c1: The live page shows one list of what needs someone and no Needs attention section, and a blocked lane's question appears in it once.

c2: The list opens with one sentence counting the items by who must act and how many hold up the finish (for example '1 thing needs the lead, and it's holding up the finish.'), under a neutral heading, with no group headers.

c3: Each row shows its lane's stop (and a wait's blocker) as the line chart draws them, a headline, a why, what clears it and 'for <age>', with the words taken from the word table and the age from the record.
c4: Holding rows come first and carry 'Holding up the finish'. The rest follow quieter. Red appears only on a stopped stop.
c5: Pointed at a copy of the word table with changed templates, the rows show the changed words, so no row words itself.

c6: Each row's meta line opens with who must act: You for the operator, The lead, or a lane by name. Rows that need the operator come first. On the page, 'you' always means the reader and the lead is always named.

c7: The lead-listener tests (LeadListenerTests in tests/test_run_delivery_supervisor.py, and LeadMayStopTests in tests/test_run_delivery_hooks.py) pass at any machine load: they set lead-wait's load threshold, or mark load pressure as seen, rather than reading the real machine's load.

V26-3568.title: Draw a setback's thread by its state, and fold long check lists in the story
V26-3568.why: The operator approved a live mock of setback threads drawn by their state, and asked to include folding long check lists, in this delivery

criteria.text: c1: A closed thread's margin line is drawn neutral, and an open thread's line stays in the held colour.
c2: The row with a thread's opening entry shows a ring on the line and the row with its closing entry an end tick, and two adjacent threads are visibly separate.
c3: A beat that names checks shows their count and reason in its line and their names only in its fold.
c4: The marks follow the story's thread state, opening and closing, so a fixture whose thread is open, and one whose thread is closed, each draw as stated.
c5: Nothing moves under reduced motion.

c6: A check's finishing animation (the arc filling, its tick or cross, the hold and the turn to the next check) plays to its end across live redraws. A redraw mid-animation keeps the animating row and queues the next result, and checks that finish faster than the animation get a shortened one, so the card never falls behind the record.

V26-3574.title: Lead each confirmed note with what was found, and fold the fix beneath it
V26-3574.why: The operator approved a mock of the round card's confirmed notes, aligned with V26-3555's findings redesign, in this delivery

criteria.text: c1: A confirmed note's row leads with its finding's summary and priority from the round that raised it. Its resolution, evidence and id show only when the row is opened.
c2: A lens whose confirmed notes were all fixed shows one collapsed line naming the lens and the count fixed, and opening it lists the rows.
c3: A note that ended other than fixed is shown with its ending named, outside any collapsed fixed count.
c4: The confirmation sentence counts each ending, naming the commits for fixed notes.
c5: When the raising round's finding isn't on the page, the row shows the resolution as its line, as it does today.
c6: The rows' and lenses' open state survives a redraw, as other folds on the card do.

finish.label: Every story
finish.text: Each of the nine stories lands on main through the merge queue, or closes with its reason recorded

finish.label: Local suite
finish.text: The full local suite passes on macOS with Python 3.11 at the base head after the last landing, inside tests/suite-budget.json

finish.label: Waits shown
finish.text: The waits and a running review round are shown to the operator on a real record before the delivery closes

approvals.text: The operator has approved delivering this plan once its lenses align, on `main`, with two lanes, each granted push and draft change requests, and the lead granted ready change requests.
The lead reads the wait templates as V26-3552 hands them off, and accepts them or sends them back.
The operator sees the waits and the running round on a real record before the delivery closes.
Raising a number in `tests/suite-budget.json` is the operator's alone.

outOfScope: A wait measured against a clock, or "overdue".
Storing waits in the record as state.
Changing how `next` ranks work, beyond taking its reasons from `waits`.
Refusing work because of another delivery's claim. Claims stay a warning.
Hosts other than the two the release projects to, and adopter-specific overlays.
Tagging a release, and applying it here.
